earlier_scan.source_named: Extinct, unclassifiable Colombian language; Glottolog lists no descriptive references

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page coli1235 (Hammarström et al.), downloaded 2026-09-17
sources.note: Classification 'Unclassifiable', status extinct, Colombia; the references section is empty (no descriptive references at all).

sources.citation: English Wikipedia, 'Unclassified languages of South America' (Campbell 2024 list) — entry 'Colima – Colombia; possibly Cariban, linked with Pijao'
Spanish Wikipedia, 'Idioma colima' (raw wikitext, downloaded 2026-09-17)
sources.note: Tertiary. States the language is known from at most two vocabulary lists of under fifty words (Suárez de Cepeda 1581/1582), reproduces the word list, cites Del Castillo Mathieu 1972 and Durbin & Seijas 1973. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Campbell, Lyle. 2024. Unclassified and Spurious Languages. Chapter 5 of: The Indigenous Languages of the Americas: History and Classification, pp. 280-338. New York: Oxford University Press. DOI 10.1093/oso/9780197673461.003.0005.
sources.note: ten words in the sources (Durbin and Seijas 1973); unclassified; no statement: nothing on stress, accent or tone anywhere in the chapter (the words stress/accent/tone/pitch/syllable do not occur); entry concerns attestation and classification only

sources.citation: Rodríguez-de Montes, María Luisa. 2016. Onomástica muzocolima en Cundinamarca y Boyacá [Muzocolima onomastics of Cundinamarca and Boyacá region]. Lingüística y Literatura (Universidad de Antioquia, Medellín) 69: 193-215. DOI 10.17533/udea.lyl.n69a08. (Instituto Caro y Cuervo.)
sources.note: No phonology content: a word-by-word commented lexicon of the 108 muzocolima words in the two relaciones and the chroniclers, confronted with 6,890 modern toponyms/anthroponyms; the only remarks touching form are orthographic (grafía Cuacua/Quaqua, Sarbe/Zarbi) and morphological (endings -pi 'poblador', -pay 'poblado', -ui/-vi/-bi 'grande'). Section 3 states explicitly that the language 'hasta donde se sabe, nunca fue utilizada para escribir catecismos, gramáticas o vocabularios'. Section 1.3 quotes Ruiz Lanchero 1582: 'hablan generalmente vna lengua en todas estas provinçias aunque en alguno…

sources.citation: Landaburu, Jon. 1999 [colophon 2000]. Clasificacion de las lenguas indigenas de Colombia. Bogota: Universidad de los Andes, Centro Colombiano de Estudios de Lenguas Aborigenes (CCELA). 54 pp.
sources.note: only that evidence on these languages is very scarce, scattered in chroniclers; listed among extinct languages; nothing on prosody

sources.citation: Chaves Mendoza, Alvaro; Jorge Morales Gomez & Horacio Calle Restrepo. 1992. Los indios de Colombia (Coleccion Indios de America; Colecciones MAPFRE 1492). Madrid: Editorial MAPFRE. ISBN 84-7100-425-9.

Rowe, John Howland. 1974 [1954]. Linguistic classification problems in South America. In Patricia J. Lyon (ed.), Native South Americans: Ethnology of the Least Known Continent, 43-54. Boston: Little, Brown. [orig. UCPL 10: 13-26, 1954]
sources.note: Nothing on stress or tone. Establishes that Rivet 1943a's Colima treatment (our works still to obtain, print-only) is a lexical one-word Carib comparison plus Simón's tribal list — i.e. Rivet 1943 cannot contain a stress statement either.

sources.citation: Del Castillo Mathieu, Nicolás. 1972. El vocabulario muzo-colima de la «Relación» de Juan Suárez de Cepeda (1582). Thesaurus (Boletín del Instituto Caro y Cuervo) XXVII(3): 413-441.
sources.note: Word-by-word etymological/ethnobotanical commentary on the c. 50-word 1582 vocabulary; the only phonetic remark concerns whether initial gu- was a Spanish rendering of a semiconsonantal w (p. 436). Zero hits for acento/acentu/tónic/prosod; silent on stress.

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1968. Classification of South American Indian Languages (ed. Johannes Wilbert). Los Angeles: UCLA Latin American Center. Colima entry p. 219, under 'Languages of the Pijao group' (Northeastern Division).
sources.note: Catalogue entry only: 'Colima - extinct language once spoken on the right bank of the Magdalena River and on the Negro and Pacho Rivers, Cundinamarca department. [Rivet 1943a, pp. 91-93; Simón 1882-1892, vol. 3, pp. 103-223 passim; Suárez de Cespeda 1923.]' Nothing on phonology or stress.

sources.citation: Tovar, Antonio. 1961. Catalogo de las lenguas de America del Sur: enumeracion, con indicaciones tipologicas, bibliografia y mapas. Buenos Aires: Editorial Sudamericana. [= searcher's cindex 9; covers the searcher could not list because the 82 MB scan was not read - verified here from the mirror extract of pp. 144-145, 170-173, 181-183 + errata]

Mason, J. Alden. 1950. The languages of South American Indians. In Julian H. Steward (ed.), Handbook of South American Indians, vol. 6: Physical Anthropology, Linguistics and Cultural Geography of South American Indians (Bureau of American Ethnology Bulletin 143), 157-317. Washington: Government Printing Office.
sources.note: classification and bibliography only; no phonological or prosodic remark on Colima

sources.citation: Rivet, Paul. 1943. La influencia Karib en Colombia. Revista del Instituto Etnológico Nacional 1(1): 55-93, 283-295 (Colima pp. 91-93).
sources.note: Loukotka's cited source for Colima; lexical comparison of the colonial vocabulary with Cariban. Not open online; a scan would complete the bibliography, not supply a stress statement.

sources.citation: Rivet, Paul. 1913. Les Indiens Colimas. Journal de la Société des Américanistes 10(2): 700-701 (Mélanges et nouvelles américanistes).
sources.note: No phonology content: a bibliographic/ethnographic notice ('Les Indiens Colimas.. sont très imparfaitement connus. Aussi faut-il savoir grand gré à la Direction du Musée national de Mexico d'avoir publié une intéressante relation écrite en 1581 par Juan Suarez de Cepeda..').

sources.citation: Brinton, Daniel G. 1891. The American Race: A Linguistic Classification and Ethnographic Description of the Native Tribes of North and South America. New York: N. D. C. Hodges. (section 'The Paniquitas and Paezes', Paniquita linguistic stock, pp. 189-191)
sources.note: tribe list in a putative 'Paniquita stock'; no language data

sources.citation: Simón, Fray Pedro. 1627 [eds. 1882-1892 Bogotá; 1637 Cuenca 'Primera parte de las Noticias historiales de las conquistas de Tierra Firme']. Noticias historiales de las conquistas de Tierra Firme en las Indias Occidentales (with 'Tabla para la inteligencia de algunos vocablos'; Colima words passim, e.g. 'en lengua Colima se llama sasapi').
sources.note: Nothing on accent placement or tone. The only phonological testimony beyond work 1: Muzo-Colima is 'llana y de buena pronunciación' (plain/easy to pronounce — 'llana' here means plain, not the later grammatical term for paroxytone), lacks 'guttural' sounds, and has no L. Same chapter gives glossed words (tapa 'piedra', as 'encendido/ardiente', curí 'guamo', paes 'morador ó vecino', marpas 'hormigas', caparra 'barrancos'; Colima = 'cruel matador' in Panche). The volume's single 'acento' remark ('Marquita, el acento en la i') is about the hispanised place-name Mariquita, not this language.

sources.citation: Suárez de Cepeda, Juan. 1581 [1912]. Relación de los indios colimas de la Nueva Granada (Archivo General de Indias, Sevilla, 1581). Anales del Museo Nacional de Arqueología, Historia y Etnología (México), 3a época, tomo IV: 505-529.
sources.note: No statement of where the accent falls. The only prosodic remark in the whole Colima record is this 1581 observation that Muzo and Colima are one language differing 'in some words in syllables and accents' (i.e. dialectal differences partly of accent placement/shape). The rest of the relación gives c. 50 glossed words (tapa 'piedra', as 'encendido', qurisy/curis 'guamo', marpes 'hormigas', caparra 'barro', vicas 'mujer', yvi 'varón', papa (reverential term for Christians), carche, caxic 'matador', toro caqui 'lucero del alba', homopaym 'cerro grande', plant names tatibuco, guerpa, chipas, cap…

sources.citation: Durbin, Marshall & Haydée Seijas. 1973. A Note on Panche, Pijao, Pantagora (Palenque), Colima and Muzo. IJAL 39(1): 47-51.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only modern linguistic treatment devoted to Colima's word list; would confirm whether anything at all about accent can be inferred from the colonial spellings (almost certainly not), and settles the classification classification.

sources.citation: Suárez de Cepeda, Juan. 1582 [ed. 1913/1923 Anales del Museo Nacional de Arqueología, Historia y Etnografía (México) 4: 505-529; ed. 1958 Anuario de Estudios Americanos XV: 583-616]. Relación de los indios Colimas de la Nueva Granada.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The primary attestation (the only vocabulary). A colonial relación; would not state stress, but is the ultimate source for the roughly fifty words.
